ledger.note: 1806: the map begins with the Free City of Bremen. The page dates Bremen's status earlier ('Ferdinand III ... granted the request in the Diploma of Linz' in 1646, recognising it as a Free Imperial City; 'In 1720, George I recognized Bremen as a free city') and says nothing of 1806; 1806 is Cliopatria's first year. The German page adds that Bremen 'war ... eine der sechs Reichsstädte, die nicht mediatisiert wurden' (1803) and was 'von 1815 bis 1866 ... im Deutschen Bund ein souveräner Staat'; the 1806 and 1815 events themselves are on no page, so the confidence stays 1. The region is the city and Vegesack, redrawn from Cliopatria's misplaced outline.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: November 1918: Bremen, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic. The revolution 'reached Bremen on 6 November 1918' and a workers' and soldiers' council 'took over the city government eight days later' (14 November); the short-lived Bremen Soviet Republic of 10 January - 4 February 1919 is not drawn; 'The 9 March election resulted in a government made up of the SPD' and the page calls the Weimar-era state the 'Free Hanseatic City of Bremen' (constitution of 1920). The German Empire page counts 'three free Hanseatic cities' among the 25 states. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

notes: REPAIR (batch eu-20-e, 2026-11-01). Cliopatria's five Bremen shapes sit on Delmenhorst, 12 km west of Bremen (reviewer's point-in-polygon test; my cell test agrees: the city's cell is in none of the shapes). They are marked wrong (1806, 1814, 1820, 1840, 1870) and the three new keyframes (1807-1810, 1813, 1827-1839) are redrawn on the gazetteer: the admin1 Bremen is one cell (the city), Vegesack a 9 km circle, Bremerhaven a 6 km circle from 1827. Delmenhorst is left to duchy-of-oldenburg, which now draws it. DISAGREEMENT with the reviewer's recipe: the admin1 Bremen resolves to a single cell (centre 8.75 E 53.13 N) without Vegesack or Bremerhaven, so the recipe minus Bremerhaven would draw one cell; Vegesack and the Bremerhaven strip are added as circles. Area: 256 km2 (German Confederation table), 255.25 km2 in 1871 (German Bremen page); the grid gives 2 cells (506 km2, ratio 1.98) to 1826 and 3 cells (759 km2, ratio 2.97) from 1827, a resolution effect. DISAGREEMENT between pages: the French years: 'annexed Bremen in 1811' and 'In 1813 ... the French withdrew' (English Bremen page) against capital of the department 1811-1814 (German page); the German mediatisation page opened for Baden says restored 1814. SILENCES: Bremen's 1806 and 1810 events, the exact date of the Congress of Vienna recognition (the English page says 'restored to their ancient autonomy ... within the new German Confederation' without the year; the German page has the Deutscher Bund 1815-1866), and the Bremerhaven treaty date (year only). Hanover's loss of the Bremerhaven strip (kingdom-of-hanover, eu-20) has no matching event. Free Imperial City of Bremen (1646-1806) needs a dossier. Gazetteer names wanted: Vegesack. Pages budget: 5 original plus 1 in the repair (German Freie Hansestadt Bremen); the Vegesack and Bremerhaven pages were reopened to check the quotes (Vegesack: 'In 1648 it became Swedish, 1712 Danish, 1802 Bremish and 1810 French', 1.7 km2, silent on 1806-1827; Bremerhaven: bought 'under Bürgermeister Johann Smidt', 'It forms an exclave of the state', silent on its membership of the free city 1827-1871). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (free-city-of-bremen_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row free-city-of-bremen -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. A free city: no abdication; the date is the revolution reaching the city's government (14 November 1918 on the History of Bremen page) and the dissolve into the Weimar Republic is dated November 1918. The Soviet Republic of January-February 1919 is not drawn.
